entities.name: Llanes town circuit
entities.description: A coherent walk from the grassy Paseo de San Pedro through the fishing harbour and painted Cubos de la Memoria to Playa de Toró, a cove framed by jagged limestone stacks. The clearest introduction to where you are staying.

entities.name: Covadonga Lakes, Buferrera and Sanctuary
entities.description: A six-kilometre high-mountain circuit links two glacial lakes, old mine workings and broad viewpoints; below, the basilica and Holy Cave sit against the cliff. This is the strongest full-day landscape option from Llanes.
entities.notes: On 21 September private cars cannot reach the lakes. Reserve from 08:00 via the dedicated platform; current prices are €3 parking and €9 per adult.

activity.accessNotes: On 21 September private cars cannot reach the lakes. Reserve from 08:00 via the dedicated platform; current prices are €3 parking and €9 per adult.

entities.name: Playa de Gulpiyuri
entities.description: A tiny inland tidal beach fed through a sinkhole. It is the quick coastal alternative when the Bufones lack the tide or swell needed to perform.
entities.notes: Choose this or Bufones de Pría after Covadonga, not both. Skip the coast entirely if the mountain day or buses run late.

activity.accessNotes: Choose this or Bufones de Pría after Covadonga, not both. Skip the coast entirely if the mountain day or buses run late.

entities.name: Bufones de Pría
entities.description: Sea caves vent through holes in a limestone meadow, producing deep noise, rushing air and—when tide and swell align—jets of spray. The clifftop remains scenic without the spectacle, but the blowholes themselves are never guaranteed.
entities.notes: Choose this or Gulpiyuri on the return from Covadonga, not both. Only stop when the bus schedule leaves enough time, and keep well away from vents and cliff edges in rough weather.

activity.accessNotes: Choose this or Gulpiyuri on the return from Covadonga, not both. Only stop when the bus schedule leaves enough time, and keep well away from vents and cliff edges in rough weather.

entities.name: Ribadesella waterfront
entities.description: An estuary town with harbour promenades, the Guía viewpoint and a long beachfront lined with early-twentieth-century villas. Choose it for an easy coastal town and lunch rather than another major hike.
entities.notes: Tito Bustillo cave is closed Monday and Tuesday, so its decorated interior does not fit the current Llanes dates.

activity.accessNotes: Tito Bustillo cave is closed Monday and Tuesday, so its decorated interior does not fit the current Llanes dates.

entities.name: Mirador del Fitu
entities.description: A roadside platform with a true 360-degree panorama: sea and coastline on one side, the Picos and eastern Asturian ranges on the other. It is primarily about the view, so save it for a clear spell.
entities.notes: Native asturcón ponies roam the Sierra del Sueve, but sightings should not be expected or promised.

activity.accessNotes: Native asturcón ponies roam the Sierra del Sueve, but sightings should not be expected or promised.

entities.name: Cangas de Onís
entities.description: A lively gateway town known for its medieval “Roman Bridge”, riverside setting and regional cheese shops. It is an easy add-on below Covadonga, but less distinctive than the mountain day itself.
entities.notes: The traditional market is Sunday, not Monday when the current Covadonga visit is planned.

activity.accessNotes: The traditional market is Sunday, not Monday when the current Covadonga visit is planned.

entities.name: Fuente Dé cable car and Puertos de Áliva
entities.description: A four-minute cable-car ride gains 753 metres into an exposed limestone amphitheatre, followed by a long descent through high pasture and forest. This is the area’s signature panoramic walking day.
entities.notes: The current signed route returns to Fuente Dé. Buy a timed ticket at least one day ahead and check weather operations that morning.

activity.accessNotes: The current signed route returns to Fuente Dé. Buy a timed ticket at least one day ahead and check weather operations that morning.

entities.name: Cares Gorge from Poncebos
entities.description: A narrow hydroelectric service path cut into the walls of a deep limestone gorge, with tunnels, bridges and exposed drops. Turning around after two hours gives the experience without committing to the full 22-kilometre return.
entities.notes: On 24 September the special access plan is active: park in Arenas and reserve the bus to Poncebos. This adds roughly 30 minutes each way.

activity.accessNotes: On 24 September the special access plan is active: park in Arenas and reserve the bus to Poncebos. This adds roughly 30 minutes each way.

entities.name: Cabrales cheese cave
entities.description: A guided explanation split between a natural maturation cave and an exhibition, ending with a tasting. It gives far more context than simply buying a wedge after the walk.
entities.notes: Because the Cares bus also starts in Arenas, give this a real tour time before or after the shuttle rather than treating it as a casual roadside stop.

activity.accessNotes: Because the Cares bus also starts in Arenas, give this a real tour time before or after the shuttle rather than treating it as a casual roadside stop.

entities.name: Potes, Torre del Infantado and local food
entities.description: A small historic town of stone bridges and lanes, with a fortified tower and plenty of places to try cocido lebaniego, local cheeses and orujo. This is the easy cultural and food counterweight to the hiking days.
entities.notes: A spontaneous producer demonstration is not guaranteed; arrange one specifically if learning about orujo production matters.

activity.accessNotes: A spontaneous producer demonstration is not guaranteed; arrange one specifically if learning about orujo production matters.

entities.name: Mogrovejo
entities.description: A tiny, exceptionally preserved cluster of stone-and-slate houses and a medieval tower beneath the eastern Picos. Its value is the setting and a short village wander rather than a formal attraction.

entities.name: Santo Toribio de Liébana
entities.description: A major pilgrimage monastery housing the Lignum Crucis, traditionally held to be a large surviving fragment of the True Cross. It adds a cultural interior to a part of the trip dominated by landscapes.

entities.name: Bejes and Picón cheese
entities.description: A steep-sided mountain village associated with Picón Bejes-Tresviso, a powerful blue cheese matured in natural caves. Choose it for a food-focused detour, ideally with a producer visit arranged in advance.

entities.name: Mirador de Santa Catalina
entities.description: A high balcony over the deepest section of the Hermida Gorge, beside remains of an early-medieval fortification. The view is excellent, but this is a dedicated outing rather than a quick Potes sunset stop.

entities.name: Balneario de La Hermida
entities.description: An established thermal spa in the gorge with pools, steam, sauna and hydrotherapy. It is the strongest genuine bad-weather or tired-legs alternative in this area.

entities.name: León Cathedral
entities.description: A French-influenced Gothic cathedral whose unusually large stained-glass surface fills the interior with coloured light. This is the city’s essential visit and one of the strongest interiors of the trip.
entities.notes: Aim around 17:30–18:30. “Last hour of daylight” is too late: tourist entry currently ends before sunset.

activity.accessNotes: Aim around 17:30–18:30. “Last hour of daylight” is too late: tourist entry currently ends before sunset.

entities.name: San Isidoro and the Panteón Real
entities.description: A Romanesque royal pantheon with exceptionally preserved medieval wall paintings, alongside the collegiate treasury. More intimate than the cathedral and arguably León’s most distinctive historic interior.

entities.name: Casa Botines by Gaudí
entities.description: A castle-like commercial and residential building by Gaudí, now a museum about the building, architect and Spanish art. It makes a useful comparison with his episcopal palace in Astorga.

entities.name: Historic centre and Plaza del Grano
entities.description: A self-guided walk through Calle Ancha, Plaza Mayor, medieval lanes, Roman walls and the cobbled Plaza del Grano. It shows León as a lived-in city rather than a sequence of ticketed interiors.

entities.name: Barrio Húmedo tapas crawl
entities.description: Move between bars, ordering one drink and receiving a small tapa at each. This is one of León’s defining social and food experiences, not merely a fallback dinner.
entities.notes: LAV remains the seated-dinner alternative if you prefer one reserved meal.

activity.accessNotes: LAV remains the seated-dinner alternative if you prefer one reserved meal.

entities.name: Cueva de Valporquero
entities.description: A guided walk through seven large limestone chambers filled with stalactites, columns and flowing water. This is a substantial all-weather excursion rather than a quick cave stop.
entities.notes: Saturday departures are currently 11:30, 13:00 and 16:30, with limited online allocation.

activity.accessNotes: Saturday departures are currently 11:30, 13:00 and 16:30, with limited online allocation.

entities.name: Valdevimbre wine caves
entities.description: A village of hand-dug cellar caves, several converted into restaurants, built around the local Prieto Picudo grape. Choose it for a long underground lunch and regional wine rather than a city day.

entities.name: San Marcos
entities.description: A monumental former pilgrim hospital with a long Plateresque façade, church and historic cloister. It is an easy extension along the Camino route through León.

entities.name: MUSAC contemporary-art museum
entities.description: A contemporary-art museum in a colourful award-winning building whose glass façade references cathedral stained glass. It gives the strongest contrast with León’s medieval sights.

entities.name: Mirador and Galería de Orellán
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: The main panorama over the red mining pinnacles, plus a short Roman water gallery ending at an opening in the cliff. Sleeping in Orellán makes this particularly good at late light.
entities.notes: The gallery is open again, but official sources conflict on late-September hours. Verify shortly before arrival and carry cash.

activity.accessNotes: The gallery is open again, but official sources conflict on late-September hours. Verify shortly before arrival and carry cash.

entities.name: Las Médulas on foot
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: Walk among the collapsed Roman mine faces and surviving chestnut groves so the scale of the workings makes sense from inside, not only from the viewpoint. Choose the route deliberately.
entities.notes: The L1 perimeter is not an easy two-hour stroll. Visitor services and marked-route access remain unstable after rockfall; check in the final week and obey barriers.

activity.accessNotes: The L1 perimeter is not an easy two-hour stroll. Visitor services and marked-route access remain unstable after rockfall; check in the final week and obey barriers.

entities.name: Palacio de Canedo winery and lunch
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: A restored country palace operating as an organic winery, restaurant, food shop and vineyard estate. The strongest all-in-one introduction to Mencía, Godello and Bierzo food.
entities.notes: Put the tour before lunch. Both suitable tours include three wines, so nominate a driver who limits or skips the tasting.

activity.accessNotes: Put the tour before lunch. Both suitable tours include three wines, so nominate a driver who limits or skips the tasting.

entities.name: Villafranca del Bierzo
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: A historic Camino town with Calle del Agua, a collegiate church, castle and the Romanesque Puerta del Perdón. It is the most attractive town in this part of El Bierzo and an optional excursion after the Las Médulas walk.

entities.name: Ponferrada Templar Castle
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: A large multi-period fortress above the Sil and the most substantial built monument in El Bierzo. Choose it if architecture and history appeal more than another landscape walk.
entities.notes: It is closed Monday 28 September, so the current Day 9 suggestion cannot work. Visit on the Sunday transfer or leave it out.
tags: Current draft extra · Move to Day 8

activity.accessNotes: It is closed Monday 28 September, so the current Day 9 suggestion cannot work. Visit on the Sunday transfer or leave it out.

entities.name: Peñalba de Santiago
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: A slate-roofed mountain village centred on a small tenth-century Mozarabic church, with an optional walk into the Valle del Silencio. One of the area’s most atmospheric outings.
entities.notes: The church is normally closed Monday, so Day 9 may give you the village and landscape but not its principal interior.

activity.accessNotes: The church is normally closed Monday, so Day 9 may give you the village and landscape but not its principal interior.

entities.name: Lago de Carucedo
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: A quiet lake formed when Roman mining debris blocked the valley, with both a short accessible path and a longer birdwatching circuit. Useful for a low-effort start or end to a day.

entities.name: Moncloa de San Lázaro
entities.region: Orellán, Las Médulas and El Bierzo
entities.description: A traditional Camino property in Cacabelos combining a Bierzo restaurant, courtyard, regional food shop and wine selection. Keep it as a comfortable lunch alternative to Canedo rather than a principal sight.

entities.name: Senda del Oso by bicycle
entities.description: A converted mining railway through river gorges, tunnels and woodland. Start five minutes from the hotel at Entrago; ride the easy Teverga descent or add the Quirós arm for UBERFINAL's longer, full-day version.
entities.notes: The route passes the managed bear enclosure near Proaza; seeing its remaining rescued bear is possible, never guaranteed. Payment terms vary by operator, so do not assume cash-only.

activity.accessNotes: The route passes the managed bear enclosure near Proaza; seeing its remaining rescued bear is possible, never guaranteed. Payment terms vary by operator, so do not assume cash-only.

entities.name: Puertos de Marabio
entities.description: A high limestone plateau of pastures, sinkholes, blind valleys, small lagoons and grazing animals. One of the best nearby mountain landscapes without committing to a summit hike.

entities.name: Banduxu / Bandujo
entities.description: A remarkably preserved medieval mountain village with stone houses, hórreos, a Romanesque church and circular defensive tower. Compact, quiet and atmospheric, but not actually a walled hamlet.
entities.notes: Fine in light rain, but the access road makes it a poor severe-weather substitute.

activity.accessNotes: Fine in light rain, but the access road makes it a poor severe-weather substitute.

entities.name: Cueva Huerta
entities.description: A major river cave with a roughly 300-metre guided visitor route on walkways and stairs; helmet and lamp are supplied. Atmospheric and genuinely independent of surface weather.
entities.notes: After 15 September public visits are advertised only on weekends and holidays. It is not a dependable Wednesday/Thursday rain fallback unless a special visit is confirmed.

activity.accessNotes: After 15 September public visits are advertised only on weekends and holidays. It is not a dependable Wednesday/Thursday rain fallback unless a special visit is confirmed.

entities.name: Prehistory Park of Teverga
entities.description: A museum and reconstructed cave environment showing scientifically produced facsimiles of major European cave-art panels, plus outdoor enclosures with species represented in Paleolithic art.
entities.notes: Open on both 30 September and 1 October; the reconstructed Cueva de Cuevas visit is currently offered at 16:00.

activity.accessNotes: Open on both 30 September and 1 October; the reconstructed Cueva de Cuevas visit is currently offered at 16:00.

entities.name: Montegrande beech forest and Xiblu waterfall
entities.description: An out-and-back route through mature beech forest to a triple waterfall totalling nearly 100 metres. A strong alternative full nature day, especially when recent rain gives the falls more water.

entities.name: Bermiego and its ancient yew
entities.description: A traditional hillside village whose churchyard contains a monumental yew estimated at more than one thousand years old. A very local, low-effort excursion for a spare hour.

entities.name: San Martín recovery evening
entities.description: Leave the car at La Posta and use the compact village for dinner, drinks and practical supplies. It is a deliberately easy finish after the transfer and cycling days.

entities.name: Santa María del Naranco and San Miguel de Lillo
entities.description: Two ninth-century buildings from the Asturian kingdom: an elegant former royal hall and the surviving portion of its palace church, only about 200 metres apart.
entities.notes: A post–Las Xanas afternoon visit is impossible on 1 October. Reach the monuments before roughly 13:45 or choose between the walk and Naranco.

activity.accessNotes: A post–Las Xanas afternoon visit is impossible on 1 October. Reach the monuments before roughly 13:45 or choose between the walk and Naranco.

entities.name: Oviedo Cathedral and Cámara Santa
entities.description: A Gothic cathedral wrapped around the ninth-century Cámara Santa, which contains the Cross of Victory, Cross of the Angels and other medieval treasures.

entities.name: Old town, Fontán and Foncalada
entities.description: A compact walk through the cathedral squares, Plaza del Fontán and market area to La Foncalada, Europe’s only surviving pre-Romanesque public fountain.

entities.name: Calle Gascona and Asturian cider
entities.description: Oviedo’s “Cider Boulevard”, a street of sidrerías where natural cider is poured from height and paired with traditional Asturian food. A food-and-culture activity rather than another monument.

entities.name: Museum of Fine Arts of Asturias
entities.description: A free fine-arts museum beside the cathedral, with Spanish and Asturian work distributed through interconnected historic and modern buildings. The best rain-proof substitute if walking or Naranco timing fails.

entities.name: San Julián de los Prados
entities.description: Oviedo’s largest surviving pre-Romanesque church, especially notable for extensive ninth-century geometric frescoes. Stronger as an interior experience than adding more monuments only from outside.

entities.name: Avilés historic quarter and Calle Galiana
entities.description: A compact pedestrian centre of arcaded streets, palaces and squares, including Plaza de España and the long covered side of Calle Galiana. The best introduction to Avilés begins outside the hotel door.

entities.name: Centro Niemeyer
entities.description: A bright white cultural complex of curved forms on the industrial estuary, with a vast plaza, dome, auditorium and exhibitions. It is Oscar Niemeyer’s only work in Spain and a strong visual contrast with the medieval centre.

entities.name: Avilés Urban History Museum
entities.description: A free museum explaining the medieval port, emigration to Cuba and the industrial transformation under ENSIDESA. It makes the visible contrast between old town, steel estuary and Niemeyer much easier to understand.

entities.name: Salinas beach and Anchor Museum
entities.description: A long urban beach ending at an open-air collection of giant anchors, steel “sails” and a cantilevered sea lookout. The easiest coastal excursion from Avilés.
entities.notes: It is close to the airport but not feasible before the current 11:00 flight; use it the previous afternoon only.

activity.accessNotes: It is close to the airport but not feasible before the current 11:00 flight; use it the previous afternoon only.

entities.name: Cabo Peñas
entities.description: Asturias’s northernmost headland, with a lighthouse, roughly 100-metre cliffs and a short coastal path. The strongest wild-coast outing from Avilés.

entities.name: Cudillero
entities.description: A fishing village hidden in a natural amphitheatre, with brightly coloured houses climbing steeply above its harbour. A destination-level western-coast alternative to spending most of Day 12 in Oviedo.

entities.name: El Capricho de Gaudí, Comillas
entities.description: A small, exuberant early Gaudí house covered in sunflower tiles and designed around light, music and its garden. The arrival corridor’s clearest destination attraction.

entities.name: San Vicente de la Barquera
entities.description: A harbour town spread between two estuaries, with an elevated medieval centre, church and castle overlooking the water and Picos. Choose it for scenery and atmosphere rather than a formal museum visit.
entities.notes: Castle rehabilitation work continued in 2026, so treat interior access as a bonus and verify if it matters.

activity.accessNotes: Castle rehabilitation work continued in 2026, so treat interior access as a bonus and verify if it matters.

entities.name: Santillana del Mar
entities.description: A compact, almost completely preserved medieval stone town centred on its Romanesque collegiate church. Stronger than a generic motorway break if architecture and old streets appeal.
entities.notes: Do not build the stop around Altamira: the Sunday museum timing is too tight after the flight and car collection.

activity.accessNotes: Do not build the stop around Altamira: the Sunday museum timing is too tight after the flight and car collection.

entities.name: Oyambre coast and beach
entities.description: A protected landscape of estuaries, dunes, marshes and a long undeveloped beach between Comillas and San Vicente. Best as a short stretch-and-scenery stop rather than formal sightseeing.
entities.notes: This is the corridor’s weakest luggage stop; avoid leaving a loaded car at an isolated roadside space.

activity.accessNotes: This is the corridor’s weakest luggage stop; avoid leaving a loaded car at an isolated roadside space.

entities.name: El Soplao cave
entities.description: A former zinc and lead mine opening into galleries famous for extremely abundant, gravity-defying helictites. The strongest formal and all-weather visit on this transfer.
entities.notes: The early timed visit is the key to reaching Lebeña before its midday closure and still having a relaxed lunch in Potes.

activity.accessNotes: The early timed visit is the key to reaching Lebeña before its midday closure and still having a relaxed lunch in Potes.

entities.name: Hermida Gorge and Santa María de Lebeña
entities.description: The N-621 threads a long limestone gorge; a small detour reaches a tenth-century pre-Romanesque/Mozarabic church in a quiet valley opening. This is the highest-value stop genuinely on the direct route.

entities.name: Puerto de San Glorio and Mirador de Llesba
entities.description: A high mountain pass followed by a short side road to a stone bear and a broad southern panorama of the Picos. The strongest landscape stop on the transfer.

entities.name: Riaño reservoir and town viewpoints
entities.description: A replacement town above the reservoir that flooded old Riaño, surrounded by steep peaks and water. A natural midway break with a striking landscape and difficult recent history.

entities.name: Hospital de Órbigo and Paso Honroso
entities.description: A long medieval bridge on the Camino, associated with a month-long knightly tournament held in 1434. A quick outdoor stop that adds a Camino chapter without committing to a museum.

entities.name: La Fábrica de Luz energy museum
entities.description: A preserved early-twentieth-century coal-fired power station explaining how mining and electricity shaped modern El Bierzo. A strong rainy-day industrial counterpoint to the Roman mining landscape.

entities.name: Astorga: Gaudí Palace and cathedral
entities.description: Gaudí’s neo-Gothic episcopal palace stands directly beside Astorga’s cathedral, making this a compact two-monument visit and the strongest destination-level stop on the long transfer.

entities.name: Roman Astorga and Chocolate Museum
entities.description: Roman walls and remains beneath the town tell Astorga’s first story; the municipal museum uses machinery, packaging and tastings to explain its later chocolate industry.

entities.name: Castrillo de los Polvazares and cocido
entities.description: A pedestrian Maragato village of cobbled streets and ochre stone houses. Its restaurants specialise in cocido maragato, served meats first, chickpeas second and soup last.
entities.notes: A full cocido may make dinner unnecessary, but San Martín still gives you walkable evening options if you want something later.

activity.accessNotes: A full cocido may make dinner unnecessary, but San Martín still gives you walkable evening options if you want something later.

entities.name: Santa Cristina de Lena
entities.description: A tiny ninth-century pre-Romanesque church standing alone above the Lena valley, with an unusual raised sanctuary and stone iconostasis. It belongs to the same UNESCO group as Oviedo’s monuments.
entities.notes: This is not a ten-minute total stop. Contacting the custodian ahead is recommended if the interior matters.

activity.accessNotes: This is not a ten-minute total stop. Contacting the custodian ahead is recommended if the interior matters.

entities.name: Las Xanas gorge
entities.region: San Martín de Teverga → Oviedo → Avilés
entities.description: A narrow path carved into a limestone gorge, followed by forest and upland meadows around Pedroveya. One of central Asturias’s most dramatic short walks and aligned with the road toward Oviedo.
entities.notes: The current “3h30 including lunch” is optimistic. Choosing this full walk means Naranco’s 14:30 closing time cannot also be met.

activity.accessNotes: The current “3h30 including lunch” is optimistic. Choosing this full walk means Naranco’s 14:30 closing time cannot also be met.

entities.name: How the Oviedo choice fits
entities.region: San Martín de Teverga → Oviedo → Avilés
entities.description: On 1 October, the full Las Xanas walk and the Naranco interiors do not fit together. Choose the walk, or visit Naranco before 14:30 and spend the later afternoon on the cathedral, the old town and Gascona.

note.body: On 1 October, the full Las Xanas walk and the Naranco interiors do not fit together. Choose the walk, or visit Naranco before 14:30 and spend the later afternoon on the cathedral, the old town and Gascona.

days.title: Bilbao Airport → Llanes
days.summary: Drive: 2h15 · 200 km · Walk: Clifftop, 40 min · Flight: 09:20 Brussels → 11:15 Bilbao

items.title: Fly from Brussels
items.description: Arrive at Bilbao Airport at 11:15.

items.title: Collect the car and drive west
items.description: Take the A-8 from Bilbao Airport towards Llanes.

booking.notes: Rental car confirmed by the traveller.

items.title: Optional arrival stop
items.description: If you land before midday, choose El Capricho in Comillas or the harbour at San Vicente de la Barquera.

items.title: Check in, then walk Llanes
items.description: Follow the Paseo de San Pedro to the Cubos de la Memoria in the last hour of light.

items.title: Finish at Playa de Toró
items.description: The cove is ten minutes from the hotel and swimmable if time and weather allow.

items.title: Dinner — Don Paco, Llanes
items.description: Cross the road to the sister hotel and eat in its old convent dining room. Reserve this arrival-night table in advance.

booking.notes: Reserve this table; no confirmation provided.

notices.title: Choose one
notices.body: Comillas for Gaudí, or San Vicente for the harbour and castle. Skip both after a later flight.

background: Your flight leaves Brussels at 09:20 and arrives at Bilbao Airport at 11:15. Collect the car and take the A-8 west. If everything runs to time, break the drive at Comillas for Gaudí's El Capricho — a sunflower-tiled folly built when he was thirty — or at San Vicente de la Barquera for the harbour and castle.

Walk the Paseo de San Pedro in the last hour of light — a clifftop green running above the town, and the quickest way to understand where you are. On the harbour breakwater are the Cubos de la Memoria , concrete blocks painted by the Basque artist Agustín Ibarrola: an accidental landmark that has become the town's signature.
The path passes above Playa de Toró , a small cove studded with limestone stacks left standing by the sea. Ten minutes from the hotel, and swimmable if the drive has left you wanting it.
Dinner Montemar has no restaurant of its own. Cross the road to Don Paco, the sister hotel, and eat in the old convent dining hall.

days.title: Llanes · Lagos de Covadonga

items.title: Park below Covadonga
items.description: Drive to Cangas de Onís or El Repelao and take the bus booked for your chosen outward and return times.

items.title: Walk the Buferrera circuit
items.description: Allow about three hours for both lakes, the old mine workings and Mirador del Príncipe.

items.title: Visit the sanctuary
items.description: See the basilica and Santa Cueva after returning from the lakes.

items.title: Optional coastal stop: Bufones or Gulpiyuri
items.description: Only if the bus returns on time: choose Bufones de Pría when high tide and strong swell coincide, otherwise make a short stop at Gulpiyuri. Skip both if the mountain day runs late.

items.title: Dinner — choose in Llanes
items.description: Keep the evening flexible and pick somewhere in town after returning from the lakes or beach.

notices.title: Must know
notices.body: The lakes road is closed to private cars. Book through the dedicated Covadonga bus platform and select an outward and return time. An early departure gives the best chance of fitting in the optional coast stop.

notices.title: Optional means optional
notices.body: Do not plan on both Bufones and Gulpiyuri. Choose one only if time and conditions are favourable; returning directly to Llanes is the default fallback.

background: The lakes road is closed to private cars on your date The access regulation applies around the clock on 21 September 2026. Park at Cangas de Onís or El Repelao, then take the booked bus. The main mountain service uses timed outward and return journeys, so choose times that leave enough margin for the walk.

Go early. The first buses run from 08:00 and cloud typically builds over the lakes by late morning. Access to the Sanctuary of Covadonga itself is unrestricted year-round and can be done in your own car — the basilica, and the Santa Cueva set into the cliff face with its spring.

At the top, the Buferrera circular takes in both lakes, the abandoned manganese and iron workings, and the Mirador del Príncipe — roughly 6 km on good paths with steady undulation, about 3 hours at a photographing pace. On the way down, stop at the Mirador de la Reina for the view back over the Sierra del Sueve to the sea.

The coast stop is deliberately optional. If you return on schedule and the sea is active around high tide, divert to Bufones de Pría for the blowholes and a short clifftop walk. They depend on both tide and swell, so on a calm day there may be little to see.

Choose one — or neither If conditions at the Bufones are poor, make Playa de Gulpiyuri the quick alternative: a small inland beach fed through a sinkhole and best appreciated with enough water in it. If the lakes, sanctuary or buses take longer than expected, skip both and return directly to Llanes.

days.title: Llanes → El Soplao → Lebeña → Potes / Camaleño
days.summary: Transfer: 2h30–3h driving · 6–7h day · Walk: Short visits + cave

items.title: Leave Llanes around 08:00–08:15
items.description: Drive directly east towards El Soplao, without the former Bufones backtrack.

items.title: Take the first practical El Soplao tour
items.description: Book around 10:00 and arrive at least 30 minutes beforehand for the timed visit.

items.title: Drive the Hermida Gorge and visit Lebeña
items.description: Aim to reach Santa María de Lebeña around 12:15, before its 13:30 midday closure.

items.title: Lunch and stroll in Potes
items.description: Allow a relaxed lunch and a short look around town. Visit Santo Toribio afterwards only if the day is running comfortably.

items.title: Continue to Camaleño
items.description: Aim to check in at Hotel El Jisu around 16:30–17:00, leaving a quiet evening before the hiking days.

items.title: Dinner — at Hotel El Jisu
items.description: The hotel restaurant serves dinner from 20:30 to 22:00, so there is no need to look elsewhere after the transfer.

notices.title: Action at check-in
notices.body: Confirm breakfast arrangements for both hiking mornings. A packed breakfast is particularly important for the early Cares bus day.

notices.title: Keep it forward-only
notices.body: Bufones has moved to Day 2 as an optional stop. Do not add it back here; the early cave booking is what makes Lebeña and a relaxed Potes lunch fit naturally.

background: Morning — El Soplao. A former lead and zinc mine that opened into a cave system famous for its eccentrics: helictites that grow sideways and upward, against gravity. Visits are guided and use timed tickets. Book the first practical slot, ideally around 10:00, and arrive at the ticket office at least 30 minutes early.

The early cave visit sets up the whole day Leaving Llanes around 08:00–08:15 should provide a comfortable arrival margin. After the tour, continue directly towards the Hermida Gorge rather than adding another coastal stop.

Midday — Desfiladero de la Hermida and Lebeña. The N-621 threads 20 km of limestone gorge, at points barely wider than the river and the road together. Stop at Santa María de Lebeña , a small 10th-century Mozarabic church standing alone beneath vertical rock. Its usual hours are 10:00–13:30 and 16:00–19:30, so the morning El Soplao slot should place you there before the midday closure.

Afternoon — Potes. Continue to Potes for lunch and a short walk through town. If you finish early and still have energy, Santo Toribio de Liébana can be moved here from Day 6; otherwise leave it in the original plan and continue directly to Hotel El Jisu.

A deliberately easier transfer With Bufones removed, all movement is now broadly east and south towards Potes. Expect roughly 2h30–3h of driving and an arrival in Camaleño around 16:30–17:00 rather than a rushed evening arrival.

Dinner and breakfast timing at Hotel El Jisu Dinner is served from 20:30 to 22:00, while the three breakfast options are served from 08:30 to 10:30. Request a packed breakfast in advance for the early Cares bus day.

days.title: Camaleño / Potes · Fuente Dé and Áliva
days.summary: Drive: 20 min each way · Walk: 4h15 · 14.5 km

items.title: Take the first available cable car
items.description: Ride to 1,823 m while the morning is most likely to be clear; confirm the 2026 opening time.

items.title: Cross the Puertos de Áliva
items.description: Follow the current signed route past the Chalet Real and down through high pasture.

items.title: Return to Fuente Dé on foot
items.description: The official circuit is 14.5 km, about 4h15, with 974 m of sustained descent.

items.title: Return to Hotel El Jisu
items.description: Your car is waiting at Fuente Dé; no taxi or second-car positioning is needed.

items.title: Dinner — at Hotel El Jisu
items.description: Eat at the hotel restaurant between 20:30 and 22:00 after the walk.

notices.title: Weather decides
notices.body: Use the clearest of the Camaleño / Potes days for this walk.

notices.title: If the top is cloudy
notices.body: Walk 90 minutes to Horcadina de Covarrobres and back, descend by cable car, then swap days.

background: The cable car climbs 750 vertical metres in under four minutes and puts you on the rim at 1,823 m, staring into a limestone amphitheatre. Take the earliest slot you can — this is the single most weather-dependent hour of the trip, and mornings are clearer.

The walk: from the top station, cross the Puertos de Áliva — high summer pasture, still grazed — past the Chalet Real, a hunting lodge built for Alfonso XIII, and follow the operator's current signed circuit back to Fuente Dé . It is 14.5 km, about 4h15, with 974 m of descent and the Picos walls beside you much of the way.

If the top is in cloud Don't burn the ticket. Stay high, walk to the Horcadina de Covarrobres viewpoint and back — about 90 minutes — and come down by cable car. Then swap this day with Thursday and try again.

days.title: Camaleño / Potes · Cares Gorge from Poncebos
days.summary: Drive: 1h20 each way · Walk: 4h · 12 km return

items.title: Leave early for Arenas de Cabrales
items.description: Allow 1h20–1h35, park there and take the reserved access bus to Poncebos.

items.title: Walk into the Cares Gorge
items.description: Climb hard for the first 30 minutes, then follow the level canyon path.

items.title: Turn around after two hours
items.description: Treat the turnaround as a rule; the return takes the same amount of time.

items.title: Stop in Arenas de Cabrales
items.description: Visit a cheese cave on the return drive and buy cheese as your final stop.

items.title: Dinner — at Hotel El Jisu
items.description: Return to the hotel for dinner between 20:30 and 22:00; keep the evening simple after the gorge walk.

notices.title: Access and safety
notices.body: Reserve the special Arenas–Poncebos bus. Carry 1.5 litres of water each; there is little shade, loose ground and no fence in places.

notices.title: Pace
notices.body: The plan is a 12 km return walk, not the full gorge crossing.

background: The signature walk of the Picos, and the reason to leave early. The path was cut in the 1940s to service a hydroelectric channel and runs for 12 km through a canyon 1,500 m deep, carved 200 m above the river with tunnels and overhangs.

Special access plan on 24 September Park in Arenas de Cabrales and use the prebookable bus to Poncebos. Allow roughly 30 minutes each way on top of the drive, and recheck current trail notices before leaving.

From Poncebos the first 30 minutes climb hard out of the valley; after that the path levels and the gorge closes in around you. Turn back at the two-hour mark wherever you are. Treat that as a rule rather than a target — the return leg is the same length and the light goes early in the canyon.

No water, no shade, no fence Carry 1.5 litres each. The drop is unguarded in places and the surface is loose in others; it is not exposed climbing, but it is not a promenade. Goats dislodge stones from above.

On the way home: Arenas de Cabrales, where the cheese caves are open to visitors. Cabrales is ripened in natural limestone caves in the mountainside — cold, wet, and thick with the smell of it. Buy a wedge; it travels badly in a warm car, so make it the last stop.

days.title: Camaleño / Potes → León via San Glorio
days.summary: Transfer: 3h driving · 5–6h with stops · Walk: 1h · village level

items.title: Visit Mogrovejo and Santo Toribio
items.description: Start with the stone village, then the Liébana monastery.

items.title: Cross Puerto de San Glorio
items.description: Take the short side road to Mirador de Llesba for the southern Picos view.

items.title: Pause at Riaño
items.description: Break the drive at the reservoir and replacement village.

items.title: Check in and walk into León
items.description: Ask for parking guidance, then settle into the compact historic centre.

items.title: Dinner — tapas in Barrio Húmedo, León
items.description: Order small, have one drink and its free tapa, then move to the next bar. You will not need a separate dinner reservation.

notices.title: At the hotel
notices.body: Request a refurbished room when booking. Ask reception about the garage before looking for parking.

notices.title: Road note
notices.body: San Glorio is the trip's only remaining pass, but it is a broad, well-graded N-road.

background: Morning. Mogrovejo is a stone village of towers and slate roofs directly beneath the Picos, small enough to walk in twenty minutes and worth every one. Then Santo Toribio de Liébana , a monastery holding what is claimed to be the largest surviving fragment of the True Cross — one of a handful of sites in Christendom granted a perpetual jubilee year.

The drive south is the point of the day. The N-621 climbs the Puerto de San Glorio to 1,609 m; the short CA-893 side road from the pass reaches the Mirador de Llesba and its stone bear, with the whole southern wall of the Picos laid out. It is a short viewpoint stop from the parking area, and arguably the best view of the trip.

This is the only pass left on the route And it is not the twisty kind. San Glorio is a broad, well-graded N-road built for lorries, with a viewpoint at the top. If the Hermida gorge on Day 3 was fine, this is easier.

Down through Riaño , where a reservoir drowned the old village in 1987. The replacement town sits high above the water with mountains on three sides — bleak and rather beautiful, and hard to look at without thinking about what's underneath.

Hotel MyPalace León sits on Calle San Francisco beside the Barrio Húmedo, only 100 m from Plaza del Grano. Casa Botines and Plaza Mayor are about 450 m away, and the cathedral is roughly an eight-minute walk. Drive directly to the hotel for its on-site garage rather than looking for street parking in the old centre.

Evening in the Barrio Húmedo León is one of the last Spanish cities where a free tapa still comes with every drink, and it isn't token. Order small, drink slowly, move on after one round. Plaza San Martín and the streets off Calle Ancha. You will not need dinner.

Reserve the garage with the room The hotel has its own garage with wide spaces and EV chargers, reached by a vehicle lift. The hotel currently lists car parking at €20 per day and lets you add it during the online room booking. Confirm that breakfast is included in your chosen rate; the published weekend service is 08:00–11:00.

days.title: León · Choose your day
days.summary: Drive: Your choice · Walk: City walking

items.title: Choose the morning over breakfast
items.description: Drive north to Valporquero, south to Valdevimbre, or keep the whole day in León.

items.title: Return for late-afternoon light at the cathedral
items.description: Aim for roughly 17:30–18:30, before the current 19:00 closing time.

items.title: Continue through central León
items.description: Add Casa Botines and the Panteón Real at San Isidoro.

items.title: Dinner — Barrio Húmedo or LAV, León
items.description: Improvise with another tapas crawl, or reserve LAV if you would prefer one seated dinner overlooking Plaza de Santo Domingo.

notices.title: Three versions
notices.body: Valporquero cave, Valdevimbre wine cellars, or a completely car-free city day.

notices.title: Book only if
notices.body: Valporquero has limited timed departures. Reserve in advance if that is your choice.

background: Astorga has moved to Day 10, where it breaks the long drive. That leaves this day genuinely open — decide over breakfast, based on weather and on how much you feel like being in a car.

Cueva de Valporquero · 45 min north. The better of the two caves on this route. The long tour covers seven chambers over 90–100 minutes, with departures at 11:30, 13:00 and 16:30; open every day until 30 September, so your Saturday qualifies. Only 30 tickets go online per departure and 30 at the desk — if you want this, book it in advance rather than deciding at breakfast. Valdevimbre · 25 min south. A village whose hillsides are honeycombed with old bodegas dug into the earth, many now working as restaurants where you eat underground. The grape is Prieto Picudo , which makes a dark, serious rosé barely known outside the province. A second wine chapter for the price of a short drive. Or don't drive at all. León at walking pace is a real option, and the city rewards it.

Whatever you do, be back for late-afternoon light. The cathedral holds roughly 1,800 m² of stained glass, an extraordinary proportion of wall given over to window. Tourist admission currently ends around 19:00, before sunset, so aim for roughly 17:30–18:30. Then add Casa Botines (Gaudí) and the Panteón Real at San Isidoro as their opening times allow.

Second night in the Barrio Húmedo Saturday is when it actually fills up. Same rule as Friday: order small, one drink per bar, let the free tapa decide where you stay. If you'd rather sit down properly for one of the two nights, LAV is on the hotel's first floor overlooking Plaza de Santo Domingo and carries a Michelin guide mention — about the only reservation worth making in a city built for improvising.

days.title: León → Orellán / Las Médulas
days.summary: Drive: 2h15 total · Walk: 2h · easy · Book ahead: Canedo winery tour + lunch

items.title: Leave León
items.description: Drive west to Palacio de Canedo, allowing about 1½ hours plus a little arrival margin.

items.title: Canedo winery tour
items.description: Tour the winery, cava and estate, then taste three of its organic wines. Reserve in advance and nominate a driver who limits or skips the tasting.

items.title: Lunch at Palacio de Canedo
items.description: Reserve the restaurant together with the tour, leaving a short gap between them.

items.title: Continue to Orellán
items.description: Allow about 45 minutes, check in and confirm current trail access for tomorrow.

items.title: Walk to Mirador de Orellán
items.description: Use the late-afternoon light for the view over the red pinnacles.

items.title: Dinner — at O Palleiro, Orellán
items.description: Eat at the hotel, which cooks from old local recipes. Ring ahead and confirm dinner for both nights.

notices.title: Advance booking required
notices.body: Reserve the 11:30 winery tour and 13:15 restaurant table together. The tour has limited capacity and cannot be treated as a walk-in visit.

notices.title: Check one week before
notices.body: Trail closures can change because of post-fire erosion and rockfall risk.

notices.title: Castle trade-off
notices.body: Ponferrada Castle only fits before Canedo with an earlier departure from León. Otherwise leave it out and keep the winery schedule relaxed.

background: Leave León around 09:30 and use the transfer to begin the Bierzo chapter at Palacio de Canedo . Aim for an 11:30 winery tour followed by a 13:15 restaurant reservation. Both the 90-minute Picantal and A Tope experiences visit the winery and cava and finish with three organic wines; A Tope also includes a small cheese-and-charcuterie pairing. Reserve the tour by phone and the table at the same time.

Tour before lunch This order preserves the afternoon at Orellán and avoids touring immediately after a substantial meal. The tasting is still alcohol: nominate one driver to limit or skip the pours, then leave after lunch for the roughly 45-minute drive to Orellán.
After checking in, today is the view from above; tomorrow you walk into it. Treat the evening as reconnaissance and don't try to see everything before dinner.

Las Médulas is what remains after Roman engineers dismantled a mountain range for its gold. The technique — ruina montium — meant driving tunnel networks into the rock, then releasing aqueduct water into them until the hydraulic pressure brought the whole hillside down. Pliny the Elder saw it and wrote that the engineers themselves were frightened by what they had made. What is left is a landscape of red pinnacles.

The fire, honestly August 2025 burned the chestnut groves that frame the site, and around 40% of them are rated poorly for medium-term recovery. But the CSIC assessment found fewer than 20% of individual chestnuts badly damaged, described the heritage damage as isolated and reversible, and named soil erosion as the main problem; the report sent to UNESCO in April 2026 says the same. Orellán reopened within two months of the fire. The pinnacles are geology and were never at risk. The live issue is trail closures from rockfall risk where erosion has destabilised slopes. Which paths are open changes — ring the Casa del Parque the week before you travel. Go to the Mirador de Orellán for the late-afternoon light regardless; that is when the rock turns properly red.

You are sleeping in Orellán — the village the viewpoint belongs to. That is the whole point of this base: you walk up for the evening light rather than driving to it, and again at dawn tomorrow if the sky looks worth it.

Dinner at the hotel O Palleiro cooks from old local recipes, some of them reconstructed Roman, and it is the only kitchen you need on either night. It is a small family place, so ring ahead and confirm dinner for both nights rather than trusting posted hours — Sunday evening in rural Bierzo is not a night to improvise.

days.title: Orellán / Las Médulas · El Bierzo
days.summary: Drive: Short hops only · Walk: 2–4h · route dependent

items.title: Walk into Las Médulas
items.description: Check live marked-route access, then choose a shorter Valiñas walk or the medium 10.5 km perimeter.

items.title: Lunch near Las Médulas
items.description: Keep it simple and flexible rather than building the walk around another timed reservation.

items.title: Optional · Villafranca del Bierzo
items.description: If the walk finishes early enough, explore the Camino town before returning south.

items.title: Return to Orellán for sunset
items.description: Ponferrada Castle is closed today; visit it on Sunday's transfer or leave it out.

items.title: Dinner — at O Palleiro, Orellán
items.description: Return to the hotel for the second planned dinner rather than trying to improvise in rural Bierzo.

notices.title: Major alternative
notices.body: Choose Peñalba de Santiago instead of the full Las Médulas walk; the narrow road takes about an hour each way.

notices.title: Monday closure
notices.body: Ponferrada's Templar castle cannot be added today. It only fits before the booked Canedo visit on Day 8 with an earlier start from León.

background: This is the day the second night was bought for. Yesterday you looked down into Las Médulas from Orellán; today you walk into it, and you start from the door.

Morning — Las Médulas on foot. Ten minutes down from Orellán. Do not rely on the visitor centre being open: check live marked-route access online and with the hotel shortly before setting out. The shorter Valiñas-area walk is roughly 1½–2½ hours; the official L1 perimeter from Orellán is 10.5 km with 404 m of ascent, around 3½–4½ hours and rated medium. Being inside the collapsed workings, rather than looking down at them, is a completely different experience — the scale of what the Romans took apart only registers from the floor of it.

Peñalba de Santiago If you'd rather go up than around: the Valle del Silencio climbs south from Ponferrada to a village of slate roofs at the head of a mountain valley, built around a 10th-century Mozarabic church with a horseshoe-arched double doorway. One of the more extraordinary things in this corner of Spain, and almost nobody goes. The road up is narrow and slow — about an hour each way — so it's this or the full Las Médulas walk, not both.

Afternoon — keep it flexible. Eat close to Las Médulas after the walk. If time and energy remain, drive to Villafranca del Bierzo , a Camino town whose Puerta del Perdón granted pilgrims too ill to continue the same indulgence as reaching Santiago. Otherwise stay near Orellán and enjoy the second sunset without another excursion.
Ponferrada's Templar castle is closed on Monday. It only fits before the booked Canedo visit on Sunday if you leave León earlier; otherwise leave it out.

Mencía and Godello You met both at Canedo yesterday. Mencía is the red — thin-skinned, high-altitude, closer to the Loire than to Rioja in build. Godello is the white, and the more surprising of the two. Neither travels much beyond Spain, which is why buying a bottle at the winery makes sense.

days.title: Orellán / Las Médulas → Astorga → San Martín de Teverga
days.summary: Drive: 3h15 · max 2h at once · Walk: Astorga on foot

items.title: Leave Orellán
items.description: Drive via Ponferrada to Astorga.

items.title: Explore Astorga
items.description: See the Gaudí palace and cathedral, then allow a long lunch.

items.title: Continue north
items.description: Take the A-6 and AP-66; Santa Cristina de Lena is an optional 35–60-minute fixed-hours stop.

items.title: Arrive in San Martín de Teverga
items.description: The later time applies if you visit Santa Cristina; La Posta accepts arrivals until 21:00.

items.title: Dinner — walk into San Martín
items.description: Use the village restaurants rather than planning the evening around the hotel. Casa Laureano is the UBERFINAL first choice.

notices.title: Route instruction
notices.body: Stay on the motorway to Trubia. Do not take the Lena exit or Cobertoria shortcut.

notices.title: Easy evening
notices.body: La Posta is on the village square with parking nearby, shops and several places to eat within walking distance.

background: The longest transfer of the trip, deliberately broken in the middle by somewhere worth stopping rather than a service station. All motorway, no passes.

08:30 — leave Orellán. 10:00 — Astorga. Half an hour down to Ponferrada, then an hour on the A-6. 13:00 — lunch, which will take two hours whether you intend it to or not. 15:00 — back on the A-6, past León, north on the AP-66. 17:00 — San Martín de Teverga.

Astorga. The Palacio Episcopal is one of only three Gaudí buildings outside Catalonia — a granite fantasy of a bishop's palace so alarming to the diocese that no bishop ever lived in it. The cathedral stands immediately beside it, and the contrast is the whole visit. Add the Roman walls and the ergástula, and the Museo del Chocolate : Astorga was Spain's chocolate town, with dozens of factories at its peak.

Cocido maragato Served backwards — nine or ten meats first, then the chickpeas and cabbage, and the soup last. The local story involves soldiers eating the best part before a battle could interrupt them. Order one between two unless you plan to skip dinner, which is the honest option.

A fixed-hours stop on the A-66 At Pola de Lena, just off the motorway on the last leg north, Santa Cristina de Lena stands alone on a hillside — a small 9th-century church belonging to the same UNESCO listing as the Oviedo monuments you see on Day 12. Allow 35–60 minutes including the approach. On your Tuesday it is currently open 11:00–13:00 and 16:30–18:30; contact the custodian ahead if the interior matters.

One turning to avoid Coming north on the A-66, do not take the Lena exit for the Cobertoria shortcut — that is precisely the hairpin road you have removed from this trip. Stay on the motorway as far as Trubia and come up the Trubia valley at river level, through Proaza and Caranga. Twenty minutes longer, and flat all the way.

A recovery evening that needs little planning La Posta sits on the village square with parking nearby. San Martín is the capital of its valley, with shops and several places to eat and drink within walking distance. Casa Laureano is the UBERFINAL first choice for Asturian stews, wild game, sausage and fabada. Check current opening nights shortly before the trip, then walk to dinner and leave the car parked.

days.title: San Martín de Teverga · Senda del Oso by e-bike
days.summary: Drive: 5 min to Entrago · Ride: 18–45 km · choose the version

items.title: Drive to Entrago
items.description: The trailhead and bike rental are about five minutes from La Posta.

items.title: Ride the Teverga arm and main trunk
items.description: Follow the converted railway through Valdecerezales and Peñas Juntas toward Proaza and Buyera or Tuñón.

items.title: Choose the distance as you go
items.description: The standard descent is 18–22 km. Add part of the Quirós arm for roughly 28–35 km, or arrange the UBERFINAL-style 35–45 km full-day version.

items.title: Use the agreed return shuttle
items.description: Pickup points and included transport vary by operator; confirm the endpoint when reserving rather than assuming collection from anywhere.

items.title: Dinner — San Martín de Teverga
items.description: Walk from La Posta to the village restaurants. Keep the evening unreserved unless a current opening check suggests otherwise.

notices.title: Before today
notices.body: Reserve the e-bikes and return shuttle. Confirm the pickup point, latest collection time and payment method.

notices.title: Full day or relaxed
notices.body: UBERFINAL makes this a 35–45 km cycling day. The 18–22 km descent remains the weather, energy or late-start fallback.

background: A full day on the bikes, and the only day of the trip where you are neither walking nor making a transfer. The Senda follows a dismantled mining railway through river gorges, more than thirty tunnels and woodland. Its three connected arms form a Y : roughly 11 km from Entrago to Caranga, 11 km from Caranga to Tuñón, and a 14 km Quirós arm from Caranga toward Santa Marina. The mapped network is about 36 km, but riding a branch out and back makes the day's total longer.

Entrago → Caranga · about 11 km. Start with the Teverga arm through the Valdecerezales gorge, where the path crosses tunnels and bridges above the river. Quirós detour · flexible. Turn toward the Valdemurio reservoir and return to Caranga. This is the quiet branch and the easiest way to turn the standard ride into a 28–35 km day. Caranga → Proaza → Buyera or Tuñón. Continue through Peñas Juntas and the longer tunnels. The managed bear enclosure is beside the trail near Proaza; seeing its remaining rescued bear is possible, never guaranteed. Long version · approximately 35–45 km. Take more of the Quirós arm and continue to the operator's agreed northern endpoint. Allow five to six hours with lunch and stops.

The shuttle defines the route Operators advertise different distances and endpoints. Some collect at Buyera, some use Tuñón, and not every company supports a free-form 35–45 km finish. Reserve the long route explicitly, including the Quirós detour and final pickup, before treating it as fixed.

Walking alternative: Puertos de Marabio If you would rather walk than ride, or cycling weather fails, use the 8.4 km waymarked circuit from the Ermita de Santa Ana. It is high karst pasture with sinkholes, blind valleys, shepherds' cabins and a dolmen near the Capilla de Santa Cristina. The final 7 km access from Entrago is steep and winding, there is no formal car park at the top, and water is limited. It does not fit beside the full-day ride.
About the ponies The most reliable free-living asturcón herd is on the Sierra del Sueve near Llanes, not Marabio. If the ponies matter, use the Mirador del Fito option earlier in the trip.

days.title: San Martín de Teverga → Oviedo → Avilés
days.summary: Drive: 1h40 · all forward · Choose: 3–5h walk or monuments

items.title: Choose the morning before leaving
items.description: Nature means Las Xanas; culture means the Naranco monuments. Their verified timings do not allow both.

items.title: Nature version — walk Las Xanas
items.description: Allow the official 3–5 hours before lunch, then skip Naranco and continue to central Oviedo.
items.choiceGroup: Day 12 morning: Las Xanas or Naranco

items.title: Culture version — go directly to Naranco
items.description: Visit Santa María and San Miguel before the monuments close at 14:30.
items.choiceGroup: Day 12 morning: Las Xanas or Naranco

items.title: Use the late afternoon in Oviedo
items.description: The cathedral and Cámara Santa reopen 16:00–18:00; add Fontán or Gascona as time allows.

items.title: Continue to Avilés
items.description: Walk the old quarter and cross to the Centro Niemeyer after dark if energy allows.

items.title: Dinner — choose around Calle Galiana, Avilés
items.description: Pick somewhere under the arcades after checking in. Keep this flexible around the Oviedo timing and the optional Niemeyer walk.

notices.title: Timing conflict
notices.body: Naranco closes at 14:30 on 1 October. It cannot follow the full Las Xanas walk.

notices.title: If it rains
notices.body: Choose the Prehistory Park in Teverga or the Fine Arts Museum in Oviedo. Cueva Huerta has no normal weekday visit.

background: Check out and drive about half an hour down the Teverga valley to Villanueva. Las Xanas sits directly on the road toward Oviedo, which is the whole reason the schedule works — you are not doubling back on anything today.

The Desfiladero de las Xanas is a path barely a metre wide, chiselled into the wall of a limestone cleft in the 1920s to connect a village to its valley. It climbs about 2.5 km to the meadows at Pedroveya with the rock closing to a few metres overhead. It takes its name from the xanas, the water spirits of Asturian folklore, who are said to live in exactly this sort of place and to be less benign than they look.

The official circular route is 9.03 km with 437 m of ascent, rated medium and estimated at 3–5 hours before a sit-down lunch. It is one of central Asturias's best short walks, but not the compact 3h30-with-lunch stop the earlier draft assumed.

If it's raining Cueva Huerta does not normally run public weekday visits after 15 September, and Banduxu's steep access road is not a severe-weather solution. The reliable options are the Prehistory Park at Teverga or the Museum of Fine Arts in central Oviedo.

The culture version. Go straight to Santa María del Naranco and San Miguel de Lillo : 9th-century Asturian pre-Romanesque buildings from the period when this small kingdom was the only unconquered Christian territory in Iberia. Naranco began as a royal hall rather than a church, and it looks it. They stand only about 200 m apart, not twenty minutes apart, and both belong to the UNESCO listing.
The choice that fixes the day Winter hours begin on 1 October and Naranco closes at 14:30. Visit before roughly 13:45, or walk Las Xanas and skip the interiors. Do not plan both.

Then Oviedo, in the afternoon rather than overnight. An 11:00 flight means leaving your bed at 08:30 tomorrow, so there was never going to be a morning in the city — better to take it now while everything is open. The cathedral and its Cámara Santa , a pre-Romanesque chamber swallowed by the later Gothic building and holding the Cruz de la Victoria; then the Plaza del Fontán and the squares around it. The centre is compact and improbably well-scrubbed; two or three hours covers it.

Oviedo's afternoon window On Thursday 1 October, cultural access to the cathedral and Cámara Santa is currently 10:00–13:00 and 16:00–18:00. Build the afternoon around the 16:00 reopening and arrive well before the final admission.

Calle Gascona before you go The cider street, and its bars open from lunchtime — so you get your culín in daylight instead of at midnight. Asturian sidra natural is unfiltered and still, and is poured escanciada from arm's length above the glass to aerate it on impact. Two fingers deep, drunk in one go before it flattens; the last drop goes on the floor to rinse the glass. Let the waiter pour — everyone tries it themselves once and everyone wears it. Whoever is driving to Avilés sits this one out.

Thirty minutes on to Avilés. A working estuary town rather than a cathedral city, and the only place on this route that isn't limestone and Romanesque. Calle Galiana is an arcaded medieval street running down to the old quarter, and the streets around Plaza de España are compact and almost entirely untouristed. Across the water sits the Centro Niemeyer — Oscar Niemeyer's only work in Spain, white curves dropped into a post-industrial estuary. Lit up after dark it is worth the ten-minute walk even if you don't go in.

At the hotel Palacio de Avilés is a 17th-century palace on Plaza de España with a modern wing attached, and guests report direct access from the hotel through to the car park and the Ferrera gardens. Two things to specify when booking: ask for a room in the modern wing , because the old palace rooms are inconsistent and one guest found theirs dated with a leaking shower — and ask whether an event is booked . It hosts weddings, and one guest lost a night to music running until five. A Thursday in October is low risk, but it is a thirty-second question the night before a flight.

background: Asturias Airport sits at Santiago del Monte, twenty minutes west of Avilés. This is the whole reason the last base moved: from Oviedo you would be leaving at eight and taking breakfast at quarter past seven, which most Spanish hotels will not serve.
08:00 — breakfast, at a normal hour. 08:30 — leave, refuelling on the way out of town. 09:00 — airport. Rental drop-off, then bag drop. 11:00 — depart Asturias Airport. 13:05 — arrive in Brussels.

The one-way return You collected the car at Bilbao and you are returning it at Asturias. Confirm the drop-off fee and the return location with the rental company before you travel rather than discovering it at the desk with a flight to catch. Fill the tank before you reach the airport perimeter; airport-adjacent fuel is both scarcer and dearer.

The hotel is 8 km from Potes and 15 km from the Fuente Dé cable car, with free on-site parking. Breakfast is served 08:30–10:30 and dinner 20:30–22:00; ask in advance for a packed breakfast on the early Cares day. Telephone: +34 942 73 30 38.

practicalNotes.title: It will rain
practicalNotes.body: Late September on the Cantabrian coast runs 18–21 °C and wet; the mountains are cooler and wetter. Assume two of your five walking days are compromised. The three Potes days are fully interchangeable — use the clearest for Fuente Dé, the next for the Cares.

practicalNotes.title: The driving, honestly
practicalNotes.body: Roughly 1,300 km before optional side trips, rising toward 1,600 km if you use the driving-heavy León and reserve options. The hairpin passes are gone. One mountain road remains — San Glorio on Day 6, broad and well-graded. The longest continuous stint anywhere in the twelve days is about two hours, on Day 10. Everything else is under 90 minutes. Budget 20% more than the satnav suggests on the N-roads and don't drive the Hermida gorge after dark.

practicalNotes.title: What you gave up
practicalNotes.body: The guided bear observation. Late September sits past the best window and one session was roughly a coin flip. Dropping it removed a two-hour backtrack. Somiedo itself then went with the hairpin roads, so the western mountains are off this trip altogether — the price of never driving a pass you did not want to drive. Marabio still offers high pasture and herders' cabins, but it now sits in reserve because the long Senda del Oso version takes most or all of Day 11.

practicalNotes.title: Pack swimwear anyway
practicalNotes.body: Not a beach trip, but the Cantabrian sea peaks in late September at around 19–20 °C — warmer than July, because the water lags the air. The Llanes coast has the clearest openings, while Salinas is possible from Avilés on the final afternoon. Keep a towel somewhere reachable rather than at the bottom of a case.

practicalNotes.title: Where the slack is
practicalNotes.body: Three things are deliberately loose: the León Saturday, the three Camaleño days, which are fully interchangeable, and the Bierzo day — Las Médulas on foot, or Peñalba, or neither. If weather wrecks the Cares or Fuente Dé, that is where the slack lives. From Day 10 onward the route is shaped by hotel arrival, the bike shuttle, museum hours and the flight. Day 11 is now intended as a substantial ride, so Marabio is an alternative rather than a guaranteed afternoon extra.

practicalNotes.title: Carry cash
practicalNotes.body: Carry some small notes for rural restaurants, cave visits and parking, but confirm rather than assume each operator's payment rules. Bike companies differ, and Covadonga parking and transport should be booked or paid through the current official channels where possible.

practicalNotes.title: Before departure: reconfirm time-sensitive information
practicalNotes.body: Everything time-sensitive here — access regulations, cable car operations, cave calendars, trail closures at Las Médulas — should be confirmed once now and again in the last week before you fly. The Covadonga regulation in particular runs to 18 October, so it applies to you and there is no version of that day where you drive up yourself.

practicalNotes.title: Planning context
practicalNotes.body: How to use this library “Current draft” means the activity appears in today’s working itinerary; it does not mean you have committed to it. “Transfer fit” marks a stop that makes geographical sense while changing hotels. Driving and opening information was checked on 9 August 2026, but timed attractions and mountain access should still be checked shortly before travel.

practicalNotes.title: Planning context
practicalNotes.body: Also suitable on this transfer: Mogrovejo and Santo Toribio. Including all four makes this a five-to-six-hour transfer day, not a three-hour drive “with stops”.

practicalNotes.title: Planning context
practicalNotes.body: Ponferrada Castle is another strong Sunday choice and is closed on the following day.

practicalNotes.title: Planning context
practicalNotes.body: Avilés → Asturias Airport No activity belongs on the scheduled flight morning. An 08:30 departure for an 11:00 flight leaves only enough time to refuel, return the car and check in. Salinas is geographically nearby but only works on the previous afternoon.

practicalNotes.title: Planning context
practicalNotes.body: Times are planning estimates, not promises. “Info & photos” normally opens an official operator, tourism or heritage page; “Map & visitor photos” opens Google Maps.

practicalNotes.title: Planning context
practicalNotes.body: Improvise All dinners in Llanes (after night one), León, San Martín de Teverga, Oviedo and Avilés. León in particular rewards wandering, and San Martín removes the need to arrange two isolated hotel dinners.
